$comment: The blast radius of deleting app/ — every tracked file OUTSIDE app/ that names the SwiftUI app, its directory, its build commands or the release artifacts only it produces. Enforced by tests/app-references.test.ts, which defines what counts as a reference and why. `refs` is a CEILING: it may fall (that is progress toward piece F3), never rise without a row being updated deliberately. `category` is what would break: build = a workflow or script that executes or packages app/; test = a bun test that reads app/ or asserts about its artifacts; artifact = names a release artifact or bundle only the Swift app produces; doc = user-facing prose that becomes false; note = a comment citing app/ as provenance, stale rather than broken; freeze = the F1 freeze machinery itself. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-retire-swiftui-design.md (F3 acceptance criterion 11: this file is empty when the retirement is done).

.github/dependabot.yml.breaks: A comment explaining why there is no SwiftPM ecosystem entry: it names app/Package.swift. Goes with the directory.

.github/workflows/ci.yml.breaks: The `app` job: swift build + `swift run kit-check` on macos-15, working-directory: app. This job is COVERAGE (171 of kit-check's 264 checks exist nowhere else) and must survive until F3, then be deleted whole.

.github/workflows/release.yml.breaks: The macOS Swift job (working-directory: app), app/release.sh, the three app/dist assets it uploads, and the tap crib sheet that hashes them. ALSO, since 2026-09-21, the notarization step's comment cites app/release.sh as the reference for notarize+staple on the DMG: that is provenance, not a dependency, and the step keeps working when app/ goes. NOTE for whoever greps: this file ALSO says `path: app` and `cd app` in the app-bundles/app-upload jobs, and those are the TAURI bundle staging directory, not this repository directory. Do not delete them.

.github/workflows/weekly-toolchain.yml.breaks: The kit-check job is `swift run -c release kit-check` with working-directory: app, on macos-15 with Calibre. F3 deletes that job only: the same file now holds the engine-calibre job, which runs the engine's Calibre tests from the repo root and never touches app/. The kit-check job is reachable only through `working-directory: app`, which a grep for "app/" does not see.

.gitignore.breaks: Ignores app/build/, app/dist/, app/.build/ — the SwiftPM and release output paths.

CLAUDE.md.breaks: The architecture section's FROZEN app/ bullet, both Swift build commands (labelled frozen since 2026-09-30, when the intro and architecture were moved to the Tauri window and the count fell from 16), and the format-defaults.json invariant that says BOTH options.test.ts and kit-check pin it (F3 acceptance criterion 14 rewrites that sentence).

CONTRIBUTING.md.breaks: The contributor build commands: app/build-app.sh and `swift run kit-check`, plus the description of CI's app job.

SECURITY.md.breaks: Names app/screepub-engine.entitlements in the threat-model section.

THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.breaks: Two live paths inside app/Packages/KFXKit (PROVENANCE.md and LICENSE) plus the Screepub.app resource path. This is a LICENSE document: a dangling path in it is a compliance defect, not a typo. F3 acceptance criterion 13.

desktop/ui/feedback.js.breaks: Comments only. The file is a PORT of app/Sources/ScreepubKit/Feedback.swift and says so, including why it builds the URL with URLSearchParams where the Swift could not. Nothing executes against app/. Same treatment at F3 as the test that cites it: rewrite the provenance to name the commit that ported it rather than deleting the fact that it was ported. This row was missing when the interface pass merged at 4e74939, where the sweep failed on the branch's own tip; added on main with the merge.

desktop/ui/tune.js.breaks: A comment crediting the Mac app's rail (app/Sources/ScreepubApp/) as the origin of the tune panel.

docs/device-map.md.breaks: "Current support (app code, verified against ScreepubKit)" is the provenance line for the support table; it stops being a checkable claim at F3.

docs/formatting-options-log.md.breaks: The options registry names Swift files as the implementing code for three behaviours and kit-check as their guard. CLAUDE.md calls this file the app's options registry, so a stale entry here misleads by design.

docs/mac-qa.md.breaks: The gate-1 QA checklist. It names Screepub.app and the flat ~/Documents/Screepub layout because its whole job is telling a tester how the shipping app and its replacement differ while BOTH are installed. The fifth reference, added 2026-09-14, is UpdateInstall.swift: the checklist now records that the updater refusal is structural rather than predicted, because the identifier pin is an exact match, and points at the ADR that decides what F2 ships because of it. At F2 the coexistence sections stop applying; at F3 the file should go, since the gate it describes will have been passed, and this reference goes with it because the ADR it points to outlives the file.

docs/release-notes-template.md.breaks: A live instruction to the notes author: edit app/Sources/ScreepubApp/ReaderRail.swift when a bullet announces a UI change. Not a record — a procedure that would tell someone to edit a deleted file.

src/cli-devices.ts.breaks: A comment pointing at RemarkableDevice.swift for the byte-identical behaviour.

src/device/remarkable.ts.breaks: A comment that explicitly asks NOT to be reworded "while app/ exists", because KitCheck still runs against it. It becomes free to edit at F3 — and should be, or it will keep pointing readers at nothing.

src/device/volumes.ts.breaks: Records a deliberate divergence from Device.swift.

src/update/compare.ts.breaks: Names UpdateCheck.swift as what it was ported from. Provenance, not a dependency: the code is pure TypeScript and keeps working when app/ goes. Worth keeping until F3 anyway, because the git-describe downgrade rule is the least obvious thing in the file and the Swift comment is where its reason was first written down.

tests/build-cli.test.ts.breaks: A comment siting the unsigned CLI "alongside the signed one app/release.sh builds".

tests/desktop-ui.test.ts.breaks: Comments only. One test cites app/Sources/ScreepubKit/Feedback.swift as the origin of desktop/ui/feedback.js, which is a PORT of it rather than a new invention. tests/export-kfx.test.ts.breaks: A comment citing Export.swift's mobiSibling(for:) precedent.

tests/frozen-app.test.ts.breaks: The freeze guard itself. It reads app/ and app/README-FROZEN.md, so F3 deletes it in the same commit as the directory.

tests/release-artifacts.test.ts.breaks: READS app/release.sh and asserts it still produces the two tarballs and the DMG, that release.yml uploads app/dist/*, and that site/index.html carries exactly three DMG buttons. Roughly eight tests fail at F3; several must change at F2 instead.

tests/update-compare.test.ts.breaks: One describe block mirrors kit-check main.swift:774-812 pair for pair, which is what makes "those 17 checks are replaced" checkable rather than asserted. It cites the Swift by path and line deliberately. At F3 the mirror loses its counterpart and the block becomes ordinary tests with a comment saying where they came from; the assertions do not change, because they are about src/update/compare.ts.

tools/build-app-bundle.ts.breaks: The DMG naming rule, written specifically so the Tauri artifact cannot collide with Screepub-macOS.dmg. F2 removes the Desktop infix and this comment with it.
